name: Ray Archive
description: Probe perimeter ports to observe deflections and infer hidden atoms
mechanic: Black Box perimeter ray inference
rules: Hidden atoms bend rays away, or absorb rays that hit them directly. Fire a ray from any edge port and read its exit. A ray with an atom immediately to one side reflects back.
Switch from Probe to Mark to place your three atom guesses. Rays cost one charge; checking an incorrect layout costs two. Solve two chambers with twelve charges each.
Coordinates and a full ray log accompany the board. Atoms never touch an edge.

name: False Weight
description: Design equal-pan experiments to identify a heavy or light counterfeit across three assays.
mechanic: Adaptive balance-scale experimentation
rules: One coin differs in weight. Choose coins for the left and right pans, then weigh equal-size groups. A result tells you which side is heavier.
Identify the coin and whether it is heavy or light. Clear three rounds: 9 coins known heavy, 9 known light, then 6 with either sign. You get three weighings per round.
Wrong accusations cost a weighing. Every hypothesis consistent with your measurements remains listed.

name: Three of a Kind
description: Find triples satisfying all-same or all-different simultaneously across three visual dimensions in a changing tableau.
mechanic: Set-style relational triple selection
rules: Select three cards. For EACH property—shape, count and fill—the three values must be all the same or all different.
Find six valid triples in the changing twelve-card tableau. A correct triple is replaced; three incorrect triples end the study.
Every card spells out its properties. Ask for one clue per tableau: it identifies one member of a valid triple.

name: Second Look
description: Alternate two complete scenes, locate modifications while ignoring unchanged objects
mechanic: Change blindness with deliberate scene toggling
rules: Inspect scene A, then switch to scene B. Three objects change one attribute between the views.
Mark the three changed positions while viewing either scene, then submit. Clear three scenes. Three wrong submissions end the study.
The scene is never shown side by side. Switching is unlimited; marks and your notes persist.

name: Fog Journal
description: Use one-cell sight and persistent hand-marked journal to collect an artifact and return, with finite lamp fuel.
mechanic: Limited-vision maze mapping with return trip
rules: Explore using North, East, South and West. You can see only adjacent passages; the journal remembers places you visit.
Collect the brass artifact and return to the entrance before 90 lamp units run out. Each successful step uses one; bumping a wall costs nothing.
Two generated mazes await. Coordinates, exits and your visited trail are always available as text.

name: Prefix Press
description: Merge least-weight messages into a prefix tree, then encode a dispatch. Optimize weighted path length, not number representation.
mechanic: Weighted prefix-code tree construction
rules: Build an efficient binary code by repeatedly merging two available message trees. Each merge adds their combined weight to transmission cost.
Match the optimal cost shown, then encode the requested message using the completed tree. Clear three dispatches.
Undo a merge to revise. Any prefix tree decodes correctly, but only an optimal tree meets the bandwidth budget.

name: Transit Observatory
description: Nonadaptive observation-schedule design and orbital decoding
mechanic: Nonadaptive observation-schedule design and orbital decoding
rules: Choose a batch of available observation times that distinguishes every listed orbit. Each world transits when time modulo period equals phase.
The exposure limit is the minimum feasible for this candidate catalog and window. Launch only after planning; ambiguous schedules spend one of three review credits.
Decode the completed binary observation report by entering period and phase. Three campaigns have different candidate domains and observing windows.

name: Specimen Rule
description: Compress labeled specimens into a nearest-prototype classifier
mechanic: Compress labeled specimens into a nearest-prototype classifier
rules: Select three or four training prototypes from eight labeled specimens. Each reference inherits the label of its nearest selected prototype by Manhattan distance: |X difference| + |Y difference|.
If equally near prototypes disagree, the result is ambiguous. Match all twelve printed reference labels within the prototype budget. Adding or removing one prototype can change several predictions.
Every slot is necessary and at least two valid prototype sets exist. Three incorrect audits end the study; complete three different feature landscapes.

name: Causal Lab
description: Diagnose and repair changing causal networks
mechanic: Diagnose and repair changing causal networks
rules: Two directed links fail in each network. Lamps use OR of incoming signals. Toggle A/B and optionally clamp C, D or E off; compare measured and healthy outputs.
Measurements cost one battery, or two with a clamp. Installing any replacement costs one of three spare links and changes subsequent measurements.
Restore all sixteen input/clamp acceptance conditions. Failed audits reveal a counterexample and spend a shared review credit. Repair three different topologies.
controls: Tap or click controls; Tab then Enter / Space. Arrow keys move within grids.

name: Parallax Post
description: Reconstruct stereo correspondences, move the camera baseline, and isolate a depth plane.
mechanic: Active stereo correspondence with variable camera baseline and selective depth focus
rules: Match all five landmarks between left and right camera views. Shapes can repeat: compare spatial positions as well as shape. Selecting a left landmark and then its right counterpart records the correspondence.
Change the camera baseline to see the parallax increase. Depth disparity equals (left x − right x) divided by baseline; every depth is 1–4. Changing baseline clears existing matches.
After reconstructing all five correspondences, focus on the requested pair’s shared depth and expose the plate. Clear four scenes with eight plates; an incorrect match or exposure consumes a plate.

name: Wave Desk
description: Adjust signed amplitudes of temporal basis waves to cancel noise and reconstruct sampled signal
mechanic: Discrete harmonic signal synthesis
rules: Three known basis waves combine by addition. Adjust each signed amplitude from −3 to 3 to match every sample of the reference.
The live table shows each basis sample and your combined signal. Match all samples and certify; clear three signals.
You have six failed certifications in total. Slider changes are free, and numeric errors reveal exactly where interference remains.

name: Question Orchard
description: Construct full-catalog binary decision trees
mechanic: Construct full-catalog binary decision trees
rules: Build a tree that identifies all six catalog specimens; there is no hidden target. Each specimen has four binary traits.
Select an unlabeled leaf, assign a question, then assign specimen labels to final leaves. Each path permits at most three questions. Constant questions cannot split a leaf.
An audit checks every specimen. Incorrect routing costs one of three credits; incomplete trees may be edited freely. Clear three different catalogs.

name: Scent Trail
description: Sample local concentration, move a tracked rover against a wind-shifted plume and sample at source
mechanic: Gradient navigation with moving plume
rules: A beacon creates a scent field. Scan reports Manhattan distance to its wind-displaced plume center. Wind and its offset are shown.
Move the rover and triangulate the true beacon; collect only when standing on its actual position. Recover three beacons within thirty actions each.
Scans and moves cost one action. Collection at the wrong position costs three. Wind changes after each scan, so account for the displayed offset.

name: Fossil Brush
description: Plan broad and precise cuts to expose varied buried fossils within a tight tool budget.
mechanic: Risk-aware excavation with tool footprints
rules: Excavate a 6×6 sediment block. Each cell has a visible layer depth. Brush removes one layer from one cell; chisel removes two layers from a three-cell row segment.

Expose every fossil cell and submit with at least eight of ten integrity remaining. The action budget is deliberately too small to brush all sediment in the sonar-positive rows: plan efficient broad cuts where all three depths are two.
Sonar gives row fossil counts, but fossils have different connected shapes. Further blows below depth zero damage bone. Clear two digs; the budget varies with the number of occupied rows.

name: Archive Edit
description: Generated dependency-constrained patch selection and conflict resolution
mechanic: Generated dependency-constrained patch selection and conflict resolution
rules: Choose a compatible set from eight patches with varying edits and dependencies. Each release permits three or four picks.
At a merge conflict, choose current or incoming value. The final working copy must match all five requirements; multiple feasible patch sets exist.
Reset a release to revise your plan without changing its graph. Incorrect publication spends a review credit. Complete three independently generated releases.

name: Lens Library
description: Calibrate an unknown lens and reconstruct an ambiguous blurred ring
mechanic: Calibrate an unknown lens and reconstruct an ambiguous blurred ring
rules: Identify the installed lens using player-designed binary calibration inputs and one sensor readout per exposure. Cost is one energy plus one per lit input pixel.

The observed image has at least two valid source/lens explanations. Reconstruct six source pixels, each an integer from zero to four; equivalent sources are accepted when they match every observed output through the installed lens.
The ring wraps at both ends. Printed left/center/right weights determine convolution. Three incorrect certifications end the study; reconstruct three plates.

name: Invisible Ink
description: Use limited spectral strip exposures and a manifest to eliminate counterfeit parcels.
mechanic: Multi-channel observation and evidence intersection
rules: Nine parcels each carry three hidden evidence bits. Only the two genuine parcels have all three bits. Scan a row or column in one channel to reveal three observations at once.

You have five scans. The manifest gives the number of genuine parcels in each row. A single absent bit proves a counterfeit; once enough alternatives are eliminated, infer the remaining genuine parcels without exposing every bit.

Every sheet is solvable within five scans. At least one occupied row has counterfeits with at most one positive trace, which can be excluded after two different-channel scans. Mark two parcels and certify; a wrong certification ends the study. Clear three sheets.

name: Clockmaker’s Cabinet
description: Three distinct causal inventory adventures
mechanic: Three distinct causal inventory adventures
rules: Choose an adventure from the selector: a stopped clock, storm observatory or flooded cellar. Their item dependencies and access conditions differ.
Collect items, select an inventory item, then use a fixture. The stopped-clock tools must be combined; the storm has independent power and optics branches; the cellar opens after pumping.
Read clues, prepare the exit mechanism and choose its setting. Six incompatible actions end the adventure. Restart or change adventure clears all progress.

name: Track Exchange
description: Cooperative cargo exchange, staged relay and held-signal routes
mechanic: Cooperative cargo exchange, staged relay and held-signal routes
rules: Choose Crossed cargo, Two-stage relay or Held signal. Each route changes the coordination problem, not only the map.
Ada cannot cross water; Bo can. Both must reach their H cells to transfer cargo. Some gates consume a key and stay open; Held signal requires Ada to remain on S while Bo passes.
Reach both E exits with the printed requirements before the move budget runs out. Changing scenario resets the route.

name: Folded World
description: Plan atlas routes through rooms that rotate and reflect your local compass.
mechanic: Non-Euclidean room exploration and orientation inference
rules: Twelve rooms have different local compass frames; some are mirrored. The room tells you which local door points north and whether clockwise local movement turns clockwise or counterclockwise on the compass.
Plan a route using the atlas, collect seals in rooms 3, 6 and 9 in that order, then return to room 0. Translate each desired compass direction into the current room’s local door.
You have eighteen moves. The travel log records actual compass travel; restart creates new room orientations and mirrors.
